clue.text: Person unknown from Douglas perhaps

definitions.note: an adjective: Douglas is the capital of the Isle of Man

parts.note: a man is a person, especially an adult male
X is the algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A mysterious stranger who may come from a town called Douglas.
explanation.walkthrough: Douglas is the capital of the Isle of Man, a self-governing island in the Irish Sea; 'perhaps' marks it as one example of a Manx place.
explanation.definitionFit: Manx is the adjective for anything belonging to the Isle of Man, whose capital town is Douglas.

clue.text: Lost doctor swallowing special rum

indicators.note: the doctor abbreviation takes the rearranged letters inside it
rum in the old sense of strange or odd marks the letters as jumbled

explanation.surface: A doctor downing a special rum and getting lost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rum' looks like the drink, but it is the British adjective for odd.
explanation.definitionFit: Something misplaced has been put somewhere and forgotten, so it is lost.

clue.text: In North Country area's very blissful state

indicators.note: very goes in the middle of the country's name

parts.note: Iran is a country

explanation.surface: Somewhere up in the North Country there is a place of great happiness.
explanation.walkthrough: The North Country is the north of England, but here the words split into separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Nirvana is the Buddhist state of perfect peace, and loosely any state of supreme happiness.

clue.text: Jazzman rings Private Pike's mum according to Spooner

indicators.note: Reverend Spooner was famous for swapping the opening sounds of words, so the two words here trade their starts

parts.note: to ring someone on the phone is to dial them
in the BBC sitcom Dad's Army, young Private Pike's mother is Mavis Pike

explanation.surface: A jazz musician phones a character's mother from a classic sitcom, as a Spoonerism would put it.
explanation.walkthrough: Dad's Army is a long-running British sitcom about the wartime Home Guard; Pike's mother Mavis is a recurring character. The swap works by sound: 'dials' rhymes with the trumpeter's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Miles Davis was the celebrated American jazz trumpeter and bandleader behind Kind of Blue.

clue.text: See 13
Leader sacrificed, forty let out in chance event

indicators.note: out means the letters are put out of their order
the leader of a word is its first letter, here given up

explanation.surface: A chief gives himself up and forty people are freed in a random event.
explanation.definitionFit: A lottery is a draw decided purely by luck, so something that happens by chance.

clue.text: Endless criticism about old philosopher

indicators.note: the shortened criticism word goes about, around, the letter for old
endless means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: stick is informal for criticism, as in getting stick

explanation.surface: Never-ending criticism directed at an ancient thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'get stick' is British slang for being criticised.
explanation.definitionFit: A Stoic was a follower of the ancient Greek school of Zeno, a classical thinker.

clue.text: Born, then died in poverty

parts.note: née, used before a maiden name, means born

explanation.surface: Someone born and died in hardship, like a grim obituary line.
explanation.definitionFit: Need as a noun is a state of want or destitution, a synonym for poverty.

clue.text: Cheap paper's latest run?

parts.note: the news is the latest information
to run a story is to print it

explanation.surface: The newest print run of a newspaper on low-grade stock.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, 'latest run' is the newest print run; split, it is the news being printed.
explanation.definitionFit: Newsprint is the low-cost, coarse paper that newspapers are printed on.

clue.text: Regularly set up roads in an Orwellian superstate

indicators.note: regularly means taking letters at regular intervals, every other one

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters of these words
the first letter of each of these two short words, continuing the run of picked letters

explanation.surface: Roads laid out at intervals in a dystopian state from fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: The regular selection is loose at the end: it takes every other letter of the first three words, then the initial letters of the last two.
explanation.definitionFit: In George Orwell's novel Nineteen Eighty-Four, the world is split into three superstates, one of them Eurasia.

clue.text: Frank is right on

parts.note: straight can mean correct or honest, as in setting someone straight
on and forward both mean ahead, as in moving on

explanation.surface: Someone called Frank is said to be correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' reads as a man's name in the surface, but it is the adjective meaning candid.
explanation.definitionFit: A straightforward person is candid and open, just like someone frank in speech.

clue.text: Football Association?

parts.note: the surface suggests the governing body of English football, but read plainly it is an association of football clubs competing together

explanation.walkthrough: The capitalised words look like the name of the English governing body, but the clue asks only for a grouping of football clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: A league is a competition grouping of clubs, and also more generally an alliance or union of members.

clue.text: Spacesuit, no uniform, ordered for dreamer

indicators.note: letters ordered into a fresh sequence are rearranged
no uniform means that letter is absent from the word spacesuit

explanation.surface: An astronaut's suit without the regulation outfit, commissioned for a daydreamer.
explanation.walkthrough: Uniform is U in the NATO phonetic alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: An escapist retreats from reality into fantasy, so is a kind of dreamer.

clue.text: Speed reduced in large town, steering clear of Congress?

definitions.note: a noun phrase in the clue's sense: the state of avoiding sexual congress

indicators.note: the shortened word for speed sits in the middle of the large town

parts.note: a city is a large town

indicators.note: a reduced word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: haste is speed or hurry

explanation.surface: Traffic slowing in a big town to keep away from the US legislature.
explanation.walkthrough: Congress here is sexual intercourse, not the American parliament; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Chastity is abstinence from sexual intercourse, which the clue calls avoiding congress.

clue.text: Host acts badly gorging Japanese dish

indicators.note: the rearranged letters gorge on, take inside, the noodle dish
letters done badly are put in the wrong order

parts.note: ramen is a Japanese noodle soup

explanation.surface: A dinner host behaves badly, stuffing themselves with noodles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Host' looks like the person giving a party, but it is the consecrated bread of the Eucharist.
explanation.definitionFit: The Host is the communion wafer, and the bread of the Eucharist is a sacrament in Christian worship.

clue.text: Is it a beastly drawing?

parts.note: the surface asks about a nasty picture; read again, beastly means like a creature and drawing means pulling people in, a raw physical pull

explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks about a nasty sketch, but 'drawing' means attraction and 'beastly' means animal-like, giving the phrase for raw personal charm.
explanation.definitionFit: Animal magnetism is a powerful physical charisma, an attraction that draws people in.

clue.text: Adult record in a sense showing equivalence

indicators.note: the adult and record letters sit in the word for sense

parts.note: nous is common sense or practical intelligence
a log is a written record

explanation.surface: An adult's diary that makes sense by drawing comparisons.
explanation.definitionFit: Analogous things are comparable or similar in some respect, so they show a likeness or parity.

clue.text: Stick it out, then abandon final

parts.note: to last is to endure or hold out
to ditch is to abandon

explanation.surface: Endure to the end, then give up on reaching the cup final.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Final' looks like a noun for the deciding match but is an adjective for a desperate last attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: A last-ditch effort is a final, desperate attempt made when all else has failed.

clue.text: Court in frame of mind to back internet business

indicators.note: to go back here means the letters are read from the end to the start
the court abbreviation goes inside the word for state of mind

parts.note: a mood is a frame of mind

explanation.surface: A law court, in the right mood, supporting an online company.
explanation.definitionFit: A dotcom is a company that trades mainly over the web, named after the .com address suffix.

clue.text: Love to be in credit for the month

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O

indicators.note: the two little words sit in the credit abbreviation

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Falling in love and being in the black for a month.
explanation.definitionFit: October is the tenth month of the calendar year.

clue.text: Old Greeks from St Pancras drunk leaving clubs

indicators.note: drunk letters stagger out of place into a new order
clubs leaving means that letter departs from the station name

explanation.surface: Ancient Greeks emerging tipsy from a London railway station after a night at the clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: St Pancras is a major London railway terminus. C for clubs is the card-suit abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spartans were the citizens of ancient Sparta, a warrior city-state of the Greek Peloponnese.

clue.text: Put honey in traps set up to catch midget

indicators.note: the turned-around traps catch, hold inside, the small word
set up in a down clue means turned upwards, read from bottom to top

parts.note: nets trap fish
wee is Scottish for small

explanation.surface: Adding honey to snares arranged to trap a little creature.
explanation.definitionFit: To sweeten a food or drink is to add sugar or honey to it.

clue.text: Guy disheartened after a game in defence

indicators.note: the trimmed guy comes after the article and the game

parts.note: polo is a game played on horseback

indicators.note: disheartened means losing the heart, the middle letter

parts.note: the word guy with its middle letter, its heart, removed

explanation.surface: A disheartened man coming off a match, defending himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Defence' is meant in the sense of a reasoned justification, as in Socrates' famous Apology.
explanation.definitionFit: An apology in the formal sense is a written justification of one's views, as in a defence of beliefs.

clue.text: Lumber covering frame of Tower Bridge

indicators.note: the burden word wraps around and covers the edge letters

parts.note: to lumber someone with a task is to saddle them with it

indicators.note: the frame of a word is its outside, its first and last letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word tower, its outside edges

explanation.surface: Timber cladding the structure of London's Tower Bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lumber' looks like timber but is the verb meaning to burden. Tower Bridge is the famous bascule bridge over the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: To straddle a gap is to span it, the way a bridge stretches across a river.

clue.text: See 3
Shoe in box for delivery

indicators.note: the answer is found sitting in the run of letters across these words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of box, all of for and the start of delivery

explanation.surface: A shoe packed in a box ready to be sent.
explanation.definitionFit: An oxford is a style of formal lace-up leather shoe.

clue.text: Comment column in The Watchtower?

parts.note: an observation is a remark or comment
a post is an upright column

explanation.surface: An opinion piece printed in the magazine The Watchtower.
explanation.walkthrough: The Watchtower is the Jehovah's Witnesses' magazine, which suits the comment column of the surface; the question mark lets it stand for a lookout tower.
explanation.definitionFit: An observation post is a military lookout position, exactly the job of a watchtower.

clue.text: Summons author without hesitation

indicators.note: without means the hesitation sound is taken away from the author word

parts.note: a writer is an author
er is the sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: A legal summons served on a writer who never falters.
explanation.definitionFit: A writ is a formal written court order, such as one commanding someone to appear.

clue.text: Russians ultimately in American airspace

indicators.note: ultimately points to the very end of the word Russians

parts.note: the final letter of the word Russians
taken as written

explanation.surface: Russian aircraft finally entering US airspace, a Cold War incident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Airspace' reads as a nation's sky but means an air-filled cavity in the skull.
explanation.definitionFit: A sinus is an air-filled cavity in the bones of the face, literally a space for air.

clue.text: Goodness associated with the unfinished story

parts.note: my! is an exclamation like goodness!

indicators.note: an unfinished word loses its last letter

explanation.surface: Virtue linked with a tale that never reaches its end.
explanation.definitionFit: A myth is a traditional tale, often about gods or heroes, so a kind of story.
